title: Automotive & Tire OEM RFID — UHF Tire Labels & TPMS-Paired Serialization for Tier-1 Supplier Programs
summary: Tire and automotive component manufacturers serialize at the cure press with UHF RFID labels engineered to survive a 170-180 °C tire-cure cycle, then read at every point along the supply chain (port of entry, regional DC, dealer storage, mounting bay, dealer inspection) to support recall traceability, anti-counterfeit channel control and OEM Tier-1 quality programs. Proud Tek supplies cure-survivable UHF tire labels (NXP UCODE 9xe, Impinj M730, Murata MAGICSTRAP), aircraft- and powertrain-component on-metal tags, and the encoding services that convert raw EPC ranges into Michelin / Bridgestone / Continental / Pirelli / Goodyear / Hankook supplier-program-compliant SGTIN-96 records.

sections.title: Challenges automotive and tire OEMs face without RFID serialization
bullets: Tire-cure press kills conventional labels. Vulcanization runs 170-180 °C for 15-25 minutes under 25 bar of pressure inside a steam-heated bladder mold; ordinary face-stock labels char and adhesives liquefy, so any RFID solution that is not engineered for cure-press placement has to be retro-fitted post-cure at a 3-5x higher unit cost.

Recall traceability without unit-level serial. When a tread-separation or sidewall-defect recall hits, manufacturers without unit-level RFID can only recall by DOT week-code batch (typically 50,000-200,000 tires per code), forcing wholesale recovery campaigns that cost 4-7x more than a precision recall scoped to the actually-affected 3,000-8,000 units.

Counterfeit and grey-market tire imports. Counterfeit tire imports into the US, EU and GCC markets are a $2-4 billion annual problem; without authenticated unit-level RFID, customs and dealers cannot prove provenance and cannot enforce regional warranty / channel-control programs.

OEM Tier-1 program compliance. Michelin (Project RFID/IRP), Bridgestone (BridgestoneIRP), Continental (ContiConnect tag), Pirelli (Cyber Tyre), Goodyear (SightLine) and Hankook (SmartLine) each maintain a formal Tier-1 supplier-program for raw tag-and-label suppliers; non-program suppliers are excluded from sourcing pipelines.

TPMS-pair workflow at dealer mounting — 8-15% of TPMS sensor mounts mismatch the tire serial number when entered manually; reading the tire EPC at the mounting bay and pairing it automatically with the TPMS sensor ID eliminates a recurring warranty-claim source.

End-of-life tire recycling traceability. EU End-of-Life Tyre Directive and US state-level retreader regulations increasingly require provable origin tracking; tires without unit-level RFID cannot be sorted for re-tread, energy recovery or material recycling streams without manual DOT inspection.

Proud Tek pre-encodes EPC headers and serial ranges to Michelin / Bridgestone / Continental / Pirelli / Goodyear / Hankook program specifications before label shipment, eliminating downstream encoding equipment and EPC range-management overhead.

Cross-OEM product flexibility. The same UHF label substrate ships to multiple OEM programs by changing only the EPC header and the antenna form factor, consolidating supplier MOQ and reducing per-customer setup cost.

faq.question: Can a UHF RFID label survive the tire-cure press?
faq.answer: Yes: but only with a substrate and chip rated for it. Proud Tek's cure-survivable UHF tire labels use Murata MAGICSTRAP, NXP UCODE 9xe or Impinj M730 silicon mounted on a polyimide or rubber-matched substrate validated for 170-180 °C × 25 minutes inside a vulcanization bladder mold at 25 bar. Standard PET-substrate UHF labels char and fail in the cure press; only specifically cure-rated labels work in this position.

faq.question: Which Tier-1 OEM tire programs accept Proud Tek labels?
faq.answer: Proud Tek is a documented supplier under the Michelin Project IRP, Bridgestone IRP, Continental ContiConnect tag program, Pirelli Cyber Tyre program, Goodyear SightLine program and Hankook SmartLine program. Each program has its own EPC header allocation, label form factor and qualification audit; contact us for the program-specific spec sheet and to request samples.

faq.question: How does tire RFID interact with TPMS sensors?
faq.answer: TPMS pair workflow uses the tire's UHF RFID label to capture the tire serial number at the mounting bay, then pairs that serial with the TPMS sensor ID into the vehicle's database. This eliminates the manual-entry mismatch errors that drive 8-15% of TPMS warranty claims, and supports the EU GSR2 mandate (effective July 2024-2026) and US FMVSS 139 TPMS rules.

faq.question: Can RFID help with tire recall traceability?
faq.answer: Yes: UHF RFID labels carry an SGTIN-96 EPC that uniquely identifies each tire down to the unit level. When a recall is issued, the manufacturer can scope it precisely to the affected serial range (typically 3,000-8,000 units) instead of the entire DOT week-code batch (50,000-200,000 units). This typically reduces recall recovery cost by 4-7x and dramatically reduces consumer disruption.

faq.question: What MOQ does Proud Tek require for cure-survivable tire labels?
faq.answer: MOQ is 50,000 labels for stock cure-survivable formats, with sample quantities of 500-1,000 labels available for cure-press qualification. For custom antenna designs, format adjustments or program-specific EPC pre-encoding the MOQ steps up to 100,000-250,000 depending on the depth of the customization.
